scenes.heading: Incremental Loading
scenes.narration: Incremental loading means processing only new or changed data on each run, instead of reprocessing the entire dataset every time.

scenes.heading: Why go incremental
scenes.narration: Processing only new data uses far less compute than a full reload each run. That reduces latency, so fresh data reaches consumers faster. And it keeps costs flat even as your historical volume grows over time.

scenes.heading: Incremental ingest with Auto Loader and MERGE
scenes.code:
from pyspark.sql.functions import current_timestamp

# Auto Loader reads only new files
stream = (spark.readStream.format('cloudFiles')
  .option('cloudFiles.format', 'json')
  .load('/mnt/raw/events'))

# Upsert new records into the Delta target
(stream.writeStream
  .foreachBatch(lambda df, _: df.createOrReplaceTempView('updates') or
    spark.sql('MERGE INTO events t USING updates s ON t.id = s.id '
              'WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET * '
              'WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT *'))
  .option('checkpointLocation', '/mnt/chk/events')
  .start())
scenes.narration: Auto Loader tracks which files it has already seen, so each run picks up only newly arrived files. For every micro-batch, a MERGE upserts those records into the Delta target, updating matches and inserting new rows. A checkpoint location records progress so the stream resumes exactly where it left off. Together this gives efficient, exactly-once incremental loading.

scenes.text: Use Auto Loader or change data feed with a checkpoint so you reliably process each record once and only once.
scenes.narration: Use Auto Loader or change data feed together with a checkpoint, so that you reliably process each record once and only once.
